name: security-http2-authority-routing-review
intent: Agreement between TLS identity, HTTP/2 authority and application tenant routing
artifacts: Owned virtual-host configuration, SNI/authority handling, proxy normalization and tenant/resource authorization.
trace: Trace connection identity and per-request authority through the reverse proxy to the final tenant selection. Identify the authoritative check rather than assuming shared infrastructure implies shared access.
experiment: Use two owned virtual hosts and synthetic tenant responses on one isolated connection; compare intended authority and one permitted mismatch fixture.
disproof: A different error page, shared certificate or 421 response does not demonstrate another tenant content or action.
repair: Align authority handling and tenant checks, then verify correct routing, rejection and authorized connection reuse.
branch_decisions: HTTP/2 connection coalescing can legitimately send a different authority over an existing TLS connection when its trust requirements hold. Do not require literal SNI equality universally. The defect is wrong application/tenant authority or an explicitly violated routing policy, not every multi-authority connection.
